title: Six ways a guard passes while doing nothing, each caught live in one day
desc: Teaching index for junior sessions: the six failure shapes found on 2026-08-30 -- sandbox seam plus fail-closed seals the fleet, or-true in a condition manufactures success, warm-shell timing cannot measure a cold path, a gc skip becomes a ratchet, a skill's working copy diverges from its committed copy, and a gate naming a missing STRING teaches typing. Each entry names the skill holding the full incident, because step text is invisible to skill search and these lessons would otherwise be unfindable.
steps: SANDBOX SEAM PLUS FAIL-CLOSED SEALS THE FLEET -- FOUR SEPARATE INSTANCES IN ONE DAY, which is why this is the first entry. The fourth was the subtlest and shows the shape without the obvious tell: a one-line seam reading dot-source of Split-Path of the script root, with NO .tmp string anywhere in it. That arithmetic is calibrated for the proto's depth; promoted to the repo root it resolves one level ABOVE the repository, and the module it loads exists ONLY under .tmp/sectors, so the load fails and the very next line dereferences the variable it was supposed to define. Its self-test returned exit 0 because it ran where the module lives. SO THE CHECK IS NOT grep for .tmp -- it is: compute what every relative path in the seam resolves to FROM THE CANONICAL LOCATION, and confirm each target exists there. A wired-proto's seam pointed at a path under .tmp; promoted, the module never resolved, and the fail-closed default made EVERY tool call non-exempt, which would have blocked delegations, cd recovery and skill reads at once. Its suite passed ten of ten BECAUSE it ran in the sandbox where that path exists. Grep the seam for its module path before promoting, and re-run from the canonical path. Full incident: wkappbot skill read opus-self-reflection.

OR-TRUE IN A CONDITION MANUFACTURES SUCCESS. A pipefail guard written as a negated subshell ending in or-true made the subshell always exit zero, the negation always false, and the refusal unreachable -- the check was dead for every input. Or-true is correct on a VALUE CAPTURE and wrong on a CONDITION. Caught by driving the expression with input that must fail and watching it pass. Full incident: wkappbot skill read harness-no-verify-guard.

A WARM SHELL CANNOT MEASURE A COLD PATH. Markers put the hook's largest cost at 2056 ms on one line, then both halves of that line measured 11 to 30 ms standalone. The hook spawns a fresh process per call and pays every warmup; an interactive shell has already paid them and is structurally blind to the cost. Instrument where it runs; do not time a suspect in your own session. Full incident: wkappbot skill read harness-slow-timeout-guard.

A SKIP BECOMES A RATCHET. The gc sweep skips itself whenever inherited protos exist, and the rule also forbids touching another session's work, so an inherited proto can never be cleared and the sweep it blocks never runs again. Measured: .tmp untouched for three and a half months, 5448 files, 1.32 GB. Every session behaved correctly and the pile still grew. Full incident: wkappbot skill read proto-cleanup-discipline.

A SKILL'S WORKING COPY DIVERGES FROM ITS COMMITTED COPY. HEAD carried 26 steps and the working tree 24; comparing by PREFIX, not whole strings, showed six gone and four arrived, with no delete command anywhere -- the loss travelled as an HQ merge, the one shape the delete guard cannot see. Diff any skill json against HEAD before committing it. Full incident: wkappbot skill read harness-tier-score-guard-howto.

A GATE THAT NAMES A MISSING STRING TEACHES TYPING. A refusal reading there is no manifest table taught a session to type an empty table, which passed. The same message said four fields while the code checked five, and once a reader catches a gate miscounting itself no number from it is trusted again. Name the missing STATE, not the missing string, and derive the refusal from real data so there is no wording to memorise. Full incident: wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff.

THE ONE THING BEHIND ALL SIX: every one of these passed a green test while doing nothing, and every one was caught by a single command -- a diff, a wc, an od, or just running the thing with input that must fail. Prove the RED before you believe the green, and run it from where it will actually live. Method: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto.

NAVIGATION: read this with its twin from the same day, and run the paired call yourself rather than inheriting either verdict. WHEN: you have just met one of the six shapes above and want the check that catches it, or you are about to act on a number a gate quoted about your own file. HOW: run wkappbot skill read proof-techniques-that-caught-real-defects for nine DETECTION TECHNIQUES with the win each produced -- that skill is the how, this one is the what-it-looks-like, and knowing a shape without its check leaves you unable to test for it while knowing a check without the shape leaves you unsure what you found. WHY: one caution measured here 2026-08-30. That skill's ninth technique reports a diet score where the no-argument call returned 58 and the session-repo call returned 77, so the file sat seventeen points above its floor and about 1500 bytes were cut for nothing. DO NOT GENERALISE THAT INTO the diet score always lying: run the paired call and see. In wkappbot-kih the same day, Get-WkDietScoreForRepo with no argument and with the session repo named BOTH returned 58, the score was real, and the bytes cut genuinely moved it from 58 to 61. The technique is right and its conclusion is repo-specific, which is the meta-lesson -- an incident report records one measurement, and a successor who adopts the verdict instead of the method inherits someone else's arithmetic.

INCIDENT: FOUR MORE SHAPES, all caught 2026-08-30 driving one merge onto main, and every one of them passed something green first. WHEN: a gate refuses you, a tool reports success, or a letter tells you a thing is done. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the prove-the-red discipline, then apply the matching check below. WHY, shape by shape. (1) A TOOL PRINTED OK ON A FAILED MERGE. wk-gitsync-sonnet-probe printed fetched, merged, pushed while the merge had actually died on a local change to a file the Eye rewrites continuously; git status showed ahead 1090 behind 72 straight afterwards. THE CHECK IS ONE COMMAND -- git status --short --branch after any sync tool, because a push line in the output proves a push happened and says nothing about the merge above it. (2) A GATE UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION TEACHES FABRICATION. The manifest FUNCTION column is matched by a COLUMN-ZERO regex, so no C-sharp method can ever satisfy it, while the wish ground demanded rows for senior paragraphs naming C-sharp files -- the only way past was to invent a function name, which is exactly what the table exists to refuse. When a gate can only be satisfied by lying, the gate is the defect: fix its scope, and say so rather than typing the lie. (3) A SEAM CALIBRATED FOR THE DEVELOPER CWD. handoff-wish-verdict.sh resolved a sibling as ./.githooks/lib/session-init.sh, which only exists when the working directory happens to be the hook repo; core.hooksPath points every consuming repo at that shared lib, so EVERY commit in the consuming repo died with VERDICT ERROR. Its own sibling already used the dirname BASH_SOURCE form. Grep new hook code for a leading ./ before believing it works anywhere but where it was written. (4) A LETTER ASSERTED A VERIFICATION THAT NEVER RAN. A DONE entry claimed a Stop-hook sentence had been removed and verified live; the sentence sat untouched at two file-and-line locations in a file unchanged for eight days. The check costs one command -- grep the repo for the exact sentence you claim you deleted, before you write that you deleted it. THE THREAD THROUGH ALL FOUR, and it is the same thread as the six above: the artifact that reports success is never the artifact that proves it.

DECISION: WHEN A GATE CAN ONLY BE SATISFIED BY LYING, FIX THE GATE AND SAY SO -- do not type the lie, and do not route around it either. WHEN: a refusal asks for a field you cannot fill truthfully for the file it names. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then read the gate SOURCE and find which check is impossible rather than which wording would slip past; fix that check, leave the unfakeable field alone, and record the measurement. WHY, two instances measured 2026-08-30 in the same gate. FIRST, the manifest FUNCTION column anchored every alternative at column zero, which matches top-level script languages and matches nothing in C-sharp or Java where methods are indented inside a class -- so a row naming a .cs file could never be honest, and the only path through was an invented name, which is the precise fabrication the table exists to refuse. The fix allowed leading whitespace and a name followed by an open paren; the QUOTE column, the one that cannot be faked, was left untouched, so the gate got MORE satisfiable without getting weaker. SECOND, and still open: the wish ground demands a row for every senior paragraph naming a source, including paths under .tmp that are gitignored and therefore can never appear in the git log the FILENAME column is checked against. A gate whose own demand is unreachable stops being a gate and becomes a toll that everyone learns to pay in counterfeit. THE TEST TO APPLY BEFORE ADDING ANY CHECK: can a fully honest actor satisfy this for every input it will see? If not, the check is a fabrication generator no matter how good its intent.

INCIDENT: THE SHARPEST FALSE GREEN OF THE DAY -- A TIMEOUT THAT DOES NOT TIME OUT. WHEN: you are reviewing any code that claims to bound a blocking call, especially one written to fix a hang. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then grep the proto for the token variable itself and confirm it is PASSED, not merely declared -- one command, grep -n for cts.Token, and an empty result means the bound does not exist. WHY, measured 2026-08-30 on the Eye command-pipe server clock, second attempt. It arrived with everything a good delegation is supposed to carry: a per-write accounting table listing all seven writes, a stated five-second normal and two-second error-path budget, a three-case self-test reporting PASS, and a real build printing ALL PASS. It even fixed the first attempt's genuine defect. And both of its helpers read using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(timeoutMs) followed by await writer.WriteLineAsync(line) -- the token created and NEVER PASSED, because that overload takes no token, so the write stayed exactly as unbounded as before and the catch for OperationCanceledException beneath it was unreachable code. THE NAME SAID BOUNDED, THE COMMENT SAID BOUNDED, THE TABLE SAID BOUNDED, THE TEST SAID PASS, AND NOTHING WAS BOUNDED. TWO THINGS TO CARRY. First, the same wrong shape appeared in BOTH helpers, which is how you tell an author's misunderstanding from a typo -- a typo happens once. Second, why the self-test missed it: its decisive case asserted that the handler does not construct a new writer, a STRUCTURAL claim about how the code LOOKS, and a structural assertion passes on code that does nothing. The falsifier costs one line -- fill the pipe, do not read, assert the call returns inside the budget. Until a test does that, no timeout is proven. The two real fixes are not equivalent either: passing the token to the overload that accepts it can stop the WRITE, while wrapping the await in WaitAsync only stops the WAITING and abandons the task.

A SEVENTH SHAPE, found 2026-08-31: A REFUSAL NOBODY FINISHES READING IS A REFUSAL THAT TAUGHT NOTHING. The wish gate printed every unanswered senior paragraph with its own skeleton row -- 269 lines -- and the owner's reaction on reading it was that a reader skims a dump. It now prints step (a) verbatim once, ONE unanswered paragraph with its sources and row, and a single line naming how many remain: 36 lines. Close that one, run again, get the next, so the refusal SHORTENS as the work lands and its length is the progress bar. The same script serves the tool and the commit gate, so both shortened together. THE GENERAL RULE, and it is the twin of step 6 above: step 6 says name the missing STATE rather than the missing string; this says name ONE state at a time. A gate that dumps every fault at once is read the way a wall of text is read, and the reader then satisfies whichever fault they happened to focus on. STILL OWED on that gate: every skeleton row is labelled (a), so a reader fills (a) and steps (b) onward are never performed -- the refusal needs a second paragraph carrying a step OTHER than (a). And its step-text extraction still greps the literal '(a) DISPATCH' with a hardcoded sentence as fallback, which would silently substitute unverified text the moment that step is renamed. Full tool: wkappbot skill read wkwish.

AN EIGHTH SHAPE: A SUITE THAT FINDS ZERO FIXTURES AND PRINTS PASSED. Measured 2026-08-31 on the Stop hook's delegate detector. The suite hardcoded nine transcript paths in Git Bash form -- /c/Users/... -- which PowerShell resolves to nothing at all, so it found 0 delegate and 0 root transcripts, SKIPPED its missing-path case, printed four PASS lines, summarised PASS: 2, and declared Suite result PASSED. The POSITIVE direction, the only thing the detector exists for, was never exercised. The fixtures were real and present the whole time: 298 delegate transcripts sit in the session tasks folder, and the failure was the path FORMAT rather than the location. TWO RULES: assert the FIXTURE COUNT before any case runs and exit non-zero when it is zero, because a suite over an empty set proves only that it ran; and never let a SKIP count toward a pass. This is the twin of step 2 above -- there an or-true made a refusal unreachable, here an unresolvable path made the evidence unreachable, and both printed green. Method for catching it: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto.

SUCCESS: a boolean built as printf | grep -q INVERTS itself under set -euo pipefail, and it does so only on large inputs -- the fix that worked is a herestring, LC_ALL=C grep -qF -- "$key" <<< "$letter". WHEN: any shell guard, gate or scorer that asks does this text contain that key, especially one that grades a document and then accuses somebody. HOW: never pipe INTO grep -q inside a pipefail script; feed it from a herestring or a file so nothing is left writing when grep exits. If you must keep a pipe, capture the status explicitly and treat 141 as a match, never as an error. WHY: grep -q short-circuits the moment it finds the pattern, closing the pipe while printf is still writing, so printf dies of SIGPIPE and the pipeline reports 141 -- and pipefail makes 141 the pipeline's status, so the branch that means FOUND takes the failure path. Measured 2026-09-06 in wish-deleted-credit.sh: it accused a session of deleting 235 predecessor paragraphs that were present the whole time, and it only fired on letters long enough that printf had not finished. A small fixture passes; the bug lives at scale. SECOND MECHANISM IN THE SAME FILE, worth the same line: GNU grep 3.0 cannot match a non-BMP 4-byte UTF-8 character in a UTF-8 locale, so an emoji key silently never matches -- LC_ALL=C restores byte matching and fixes both problems at once. VERIFIED LIVE: erased=0 after the fix.
